# Lab workstream board, 2026-10-04 (\~01:20Z), R-C227

**How this was made.** The lab seat on neo assembled this during S6 hygiene. Sources: TIN-3692 comments from 00:47Z to 00:55Z, `gh pr list` on xoxd-ai/lab and xoxd-ai/agent-switchboard, the neo `git worktree list`, and the S6 census note. It supersedes the 2026-10-03 R-C209 board.

**Legend.**

* **V**: verified by this seat at about 01:15Z.
* **R**: reported in a TIN-3692 comment or a sprint relay.
* Times are UTC.

## Holds

* **CNPG window on honey: LIFTED** (**V**). The flag `~/.local/state/tinyland/lab-seat/cnpg-hold-lifted` exists. The blahaj seat reported the window done at 00:51Z: cloudnative-pg 1.30.1 and plugin-barman-cloud v0.15.0 in `cnpg-system`, receipt on TIN-5136 (**R**). Host steps that had been deferred to after the window may now run, subject to each sprint's own rulings.
* **R-C232: one batched neo HM switch, at the end of the sprint session** (**R**). It waits for these to be merged on main:
  * the S4 nested tmux prefix;
  * the S5 items;
  * the R-C231 gpg-agent launch at login (#2168).

  The operator picks the moment, and the switch is receipted. There are no per-PR switches on neo until then.

## Rulings R-C227 to R-C230 (operator interview, 2026-10-04, TIN-3692 comment acacd7cd)

* **R-C227:** run six parallel sprints, S1 to S6 (below).
* **R-C228:** agent-switchboard #7 lands this way:
  * validate the Rust tests and `just release-check` on sting;
  * then admin merge (the R-C11 pattern).

  There is no merge_group dispatch on GF runners.
* **R-C229:** the switchboard's formal stack is Dhall plus Haskell, model-based:
  * Dhall types for `owners.json` and `approved-broker.json`, rendered and checked in CI;
  * a quickcheck-dynamic state-machine model that drives the live broker API.

  TLA+ is added only if this cannot settle a race. The estate question (#1301 vs #1311) stays open.
  * **Operator remark, 2026-10-04.** This is context, not a new ruling. The lab already uses Dhall with the flake extensively. The operator prefers QuickCheck because it gives simple, parsimonious properties instead of extensive architecture-boundary checks. Read R-C229 in that light: reuse the existing Dhall-with-flake patterns, and favour a few properties over boundary-check scaffolding.
* **R-C230:** hygiene is salvage-first:
  * every dirty tree is pushed as a branch, or patch-archived, before it is reaped;
  * lab and GF only, because the blahaj seat reaps blahaj;
  * the stale-PR close list goes to the operator, and nothing is closed until then (TIN-3577).
* Related, same session:
  * **R-C231:** gpg-agent launches at login via `nix/home-manager/gpg.nix`.
  * **R-C232:** the batched neo switch above.

## Sprints

| Sprint | Scope | Owner | Repo / worktree / branch | State | Next |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| S1 | Switchboard, landed in full (TIN-4655) | lab seat, S1 subagent | `~/git/lab-s1-switchboard-vendor-20261004`, `feat/tin-4655-switchboard-vendor-union-20261004`; agent-switchboard #3 to #7 | **V**: agent-switchboard #3 to #7 OPEN; the lab vendor-union branch exists, PR not seen. Lab #2095, #2087, #1947, #1963 and #1964 open (protected) | Sting validation, then admin merge of #7 (R-C228); the Dhall/QuickCheck model (R-C229) |
| S2 | Platform P1: OpenBao, Keycloak, portable seat, devcontainer, Codespaces; the codex ratty rootless fix (TIN-5150, TIN-4215) | lab seat, S2 subagent; blahaj seat for cluster parts | `docs/tin-5150-s2-packet-20261004` (#2165); `fix/tin-4215-ratty-rootless-unpack-20261004` (#2167) | **V**: #2165 and #2167 OPEN. Drafts #2102, #2093, #2028, #2027 and #2005 open (protected) | Commissioning packet review; the Keycloak admin custody carrier is still unknown |
| S3 | tinyland-cleanup v0.4.2 and vendoring (TIN-3342) | lab seat, S3 subagent | tinyland-cleanup checkouts (protected) | **R**: in flight; no lab PR seen by this seat | Pin v0.4.2 in lab after the upstream release |
| S4 | cmux, tmux, nested terminals | lab seat, S4 subagent | not seen in the lab worktree list | **R**: the nested tmux prefix is in flight; it gates R-C232 | Land, then fold into the batched neo switch |
| S5 | Waifu completion with blahaj (TIN-4642); voter zram; main CI reds; hashed lock; Codex handoff branch; gpg-agent (R-C231) | lab seat, S5 subagents | #2164 and #2166 MERGED; #2162 voter zram, #2169 CI reds, #2161 hashed lock, #2163 handoff note, #2168 gpg-agent all OPEN | **V** as listed. Dependabot #2154 (cryptography 50) is held with the hashed-lock work | Land the open items (admin merge after sting validation, R-C11/R-C30); they gate R-C232 |
| S6 | Estate hygiene (R-C230, TIN-4296, TIN-3577) | lab seat, S6 subagents | `~/git/lab-s6-hygiene-20261004`, `docs/s6-hygiene-20261004` (#2170) | **V**: census done; 98 `salvage/*` branches pushed and 4 patch-only; 119 clean worktrees reaped (lab 141 to 58, GF 65 to 28); 27 dirty trees left. Stale lab PR close LIST appended for operator review, nothing closed. Linear: TIN-5328, TIN-5330 and TIN-5358 moved to Done (blahaj #1793, #1794 and #1797 merged); TIN-4646, TIN-4623 and TIN-4589 moved to Done (blahaj #1579, #1570 and #1563 merged, docs-only acceptance); TIN-2057 due date moved to 10-11 | Operator reviews the close list; next is the 27 dirty trees |

## Delivery snapshot

* **origin/main:** `e9509c6ea` at the start of the session, then #2164 and #2166 merged (**V**).
* **Neo:** gen 75 at `a9a176402` (R-C226, 23:32Z). Rebooted 19:57 EDT. The next switch is the R-C232 batch (**R**).
* **Sting:** quota 1115 GiB plus local-path 324 GiB, applied by #2159 (**V**, merged).
* **Honey:** CNPG installed (**R**). Canary disk floor: not re-checked this pass.
* **Not re-verified this pass:** yoga, PZM, mbp-13.

## Operator decisions open

1. Review the S6 stale lab PR close list (in the S6 note on #2170). Nothing closes until you select (TIN-3577).
2. The moment for the R-C232 neo switch.
3. The Keycloak admin custody carrier (S2).
4. What to do with the 27 dirty worktrees that are left after salvage.

## 2026-10-04 ~06:40Z: lab seat (neo), R-C278 and R-C281 receipt

**R-C278 (done).**
- **Pre-check:** no nix build was running on PZM, and no tmux server was up.
- **Upgrade:** PZM's Determinate Nix went from 3.22.5 to 3.23.0 through the supported `determinate-nixd upgrade` path, using PZM's host-local become file. The upgrade restarted the daemon. There was no reboot, no mount change and no /etc/nix edit.
- **Verified afterwards:**
  - determinate-nixd daemon and client report 3.23.0.
  - `nix --version` reports Determinate Nix 3.23.0 / 2.35.2.
  - `nix store info` returns daemon, Trusted 1.
  - A trivial derivation built with `--max-jobs 1 --cores 2` produced an output containing `ok`.
  - `/nix` is still `/dev/disk7s1` with UUID `DEF3D5D9-DC6A-4630-A436-CE476163D3B9`.

**R-C281:** opened TIN-5393, "PZM USB /nix APFS flush stalls (observation)". It is observation only: no remount or reboot, and the watchdog doctrine is unchanged.

**Agent note:** `docs/agent-notes/2026-10-04-TIN-3692-r-c278-pzm-determinate-upgrade.md` is written on the lab working tree but not yet committed.

## 2026-10-04 ~06:35Z: lab seat (neo), R-C278..R-C281 (operator interview, after the S15 PZM investigation)

**S15 findings (not proven; leading hypothesis):**
- **Race:** a builder-start handshake race in Determinate Nix 3.22.5 on macOS. An output from a build reported as failed actually existed.
- **Over-parallelism:** PZM's HM user nix.conf tail (`max-jobs = auto` / `cores = 0`) overrides the 2026-09-12 bound of 1 job / 2 cores, and [host-local user redacted] is a trusted user, so PZM ran up to 10 parallel builds.
- **Storage stalls:** multi-second APFS flush stalls on the USB `/nix` (disk7), up to 5 s, appear in both failure windows.
- **Signing:** key `pzm-nix-closure-1` is provisioned and its custody is correct.

**Rulings:**
- **R-C278:** upgrade Determinate Nix on PZM from 3.22.5 to 3.23.0 now, through the supported `determinate-nixd upgrade` path. This restarts the nix-daemon. Check first that no build is running on PZM; no reboot.
- **R-C279:** restore PZM's declared bound by setting `tinyland.host.nix = { maxJobs = 1; cores = 2; }` for petting-zoo-mini, plus a flake test that PZM's rendered nix.conf ends with max-jobs 1 / cores 2. Deliver it with a PZM HM switch. No Darwin system switch and no /etc/nix edit.
- **R-C280:** run the serialized PZM GC to clear the garbage from the failed builds. Then retry the neo HM build on PZM with `--max-jobs 1 --cores 2 --keep-going`, retrying a single failed derivation once. Sign it with the managed key through the existing sign task (`neo-hm-remote-producer` sign mode), `nix copy` it to neo, add a GC root, and repoint the two hook entries (R-C251).
- **R-C281:** track the PZM USB APFS flush stalls as their own storage-health item, observation only. No remount or reboot, and the watchdog doctrine is unchanged.

## 2026-10-04 ~06:20Z: lab seat (neo), R-C277 (operator interview)

**Trigger:** the operator ran `just deploy honey …` from neo, and it failed at "Gather facts after credentials loaded" with "Incorrect sudo password". The cause is AGENTS.md's per-host become rule: neo's `BECOME_PASSWORD_FILE` is neo's own credential. sting and bumble happen to match it, honey does not. `just host-sops-sudo-check honey` returns PASS for honey's host-local sops become material.

**R-C277:** fix the neo-side recipe so `just deploy <host>` from neo authenticates become with **the target host's own** become file.
- **Preferred design:** the password never leaves the host. Reuse the `just remote-sudo` mechanism (`sudo -A` with an askpass that reads the host-local `~/.config/sops-nix/secrets/become/password` on the target).
- **Fallback:** if Ansible's sudo plugin can't do that, fetch the password per run into a 0600 file that is removed on exit, with the password never in argv, never in a log and never stored.
- **Scope of the change:** neo's own credential is no longer sent to other hosts. Tests come with it.
- **After it lands:** re-run the operator's honey deploy.

## 2026-10-04 ~05:50Z: lab seat (neo), R-C272 (operator interview)

**What happened:** the R-C271 build on neo exited silently during evaluation after about 4 minutes. Swap went from 6.2 to 6.5 of 7.2 GiB. This was probably memory pressure, but that is not verified. No output was produced and nothing changed. Neo's HM eval exceeding memory blocks both the hook delivery and the R-C232 batched switch.

**R-C272:** fix the PZM daemon first, then use PZM as the builder for neo.

**PZM symptoms:**
- Builds fail at build-environment startup with "while waiting for the build environment … to initialize … unexpected EOF reading a line". It happens on a different derivation each time; the build dir is `/nix/var/tinyland/nix-build-dir`.
- PZM's nix.conf has no `secret-key-files`, so its outputs are unsigned, and neo enforces `require-sigs`. The ratified managed PZM signing key must sign in a separate privileged phase (2026-09-09 ruling).
- `/nix` is at about 4.5 GiB free after the failed builds' garbage.

**Constraints, per AGENTS.md PZM doctrine:** Determinate owns `nix.conf`. Do not restart the Nix daemon without a ruling. No mount changes, no reboots, no GF services. Investigation is read-only first; any fix gets its own ruling.

## 2026-10-04 ~05:40Z: lab seat (neo), R-C271 (operator interview)

**R-C271:** deliver the R-C249 ManagedOOM carve-out (#2181, 7cc57d689) to neo without a switch, by building on neo itself.

**Why not PZM:** PZM's nix-daemon fails when starting build environments ("unexpected EOF reading a line"). PZM also does not sign its outputs, and neo requires signatures.

**Steps:**
1. Build the `jess@macbook-neo` HM activation package on neo under the reason-carrying hatch `TINYLAND_ALLOW_LOCAL_BUILD="R-C271 hook delivery without switch"`, with `--max-jobs 1 --cores 2`, detached, logging to its own file.
2. Never run activate.
3. Add a GC root for the result.
4. Compare the old and new hooks with probes.
5. Repoint only the Claude PreToolUse agent-process hook and the git pre-commit symlink (R-C251).

**Also landed:** S11 (R-C258). Sting's user.slice now has MemoryMin=1G live: memory.min reads 1073741824. Merged as #2186 and #2188, delivered with `just deploy sting memory-guards` (daemon-reload only).

2026-10-04 ~04:38Z, lab#2140 (R-N11 guard false match on `bazelisk shutdown`). Reply to the lab seat's note.

- **The branch already carries current main.** It was updated through GitHub with a merge, not a rebase (`9acee11f`, ~04:30Z, no force-push). The history includes #2169 (codex_global_agents export), #2177 (R-C243 quoted grep patterns), #2178 and #2181 (R-C249 ManagedOOM). It merged with no conflicts in `scripts/validation/agent-process-safety-audit.py`.
- **The PR's tests pass against the merged audit:** `tests/unit/test_agent_process_safety_audit.py`, 82 passed, run locally on `9acee11f`.
- **The net diff is still three files:** the audit script, its unit test and the TIN-3692 agent note.
- **CI on `9acee11f` is queued** (Bazel Build, Validate). Per the lab seat, main's remaining red is #2175 (fleet_switch_control_plane sandbox tmp), which this PR doesn't touch.
- Merging stays Jess's decision. Nothing else changed on lab.

## 2026-10-04 ~04:55Z: lab seat (neo), R-C259 and R-C260 (operator interview)

**R-C259 (TIN-5268 preservation hold, relayed by the blahaj seat).** Sting's tinyland-cleanup keeps zstd compression of Codex `archived_sessions` (`nix/hosts/sting.nix`, `agentTranscriptCompression`, 30d).
- Operator ruling: lossless zstd is compatible with the hold.
- The hold forbids deletion, ageing out and lossy compression. No lab lane deletes or ages out agent session stores.

**R-C260 (nested tmux prefix; S4 #2182 reworked).** C-a stays the prefix on every host, consistent with R11: C-b is Emacs backward-char in eGreg. From the outer seat, C-a C-a reaches the inner sting tmux via send-prefix. #2182 is reworked to that.

**Standing operator direction attached to R-C260:** every change to key bindings updates, in the same PR:
- the console and prompt-pulse printouts: the `hints.toml` cheatsheet that `prompt-pulse welcome` renders, and the welcome card;
- the keybinding SSOTs: `nix/modules/terminals/tmux.nix`, the cmux and Ghostty keybinds in `nix/home-manager/cmux.nix`, and `docs/operations/REMOTE_DEV_WORKFLOW.md`.

**Also:** lab#2140 (bazelisk shutdown R-N11 match), from the xoruby seat on sting: the main-red causes it reported were fixed by #2169 (01:45Z) and #2178. #2140 needs a rebase onto main, which since gained #2177 and #2181 in the same audit file.

## 2026-10-04 ~04:35Z: lab seat (neo), R-C257 (operator interview)

**Background (R-C256).** The PZM GC ran through `just pzm-serialized-nix-gc` and freed only 3.4 MiB. Every profile was already current-only. `/nix` is 2.22 GiB free, 97% full.

**R-C257** frees space on PZM's USB `/nix` so the R-C254 hook build can run:
1. Remove the stale GC root `~/.local/state/tinyland/home-manager-candidates/neo/1626f9311516f9bda433ccdf595982d37fccddf0-jess@macbook-neo` (Sep 30; nothing current uses it). About 5.6 GiB.
2. Trim the disposable Bazel cache at `/nix/var/tinyland/user/bazel` (about 11 GiB), following the PZM cache-recovery ruling of 2026-09-10. Prefer `bazel clean --expunge` in its workspaces, or the disk and repository caches only. Credentials and non-reproducible state stay untouched.
3. Run the serialized GC again.

Then run the R-C254 build, the `nix copy` to neo, and the two-entry repoint.

**S8b delivered.** #2183 merged (21484e31) and #2184 merged. Sting Home Manager is now gen 110. Live slice: MemoryHigh 14G, MemoryMax 18G, CPUWeight 50, no IOWeight. A `020G` request is refused.

## 2026-10-04 ~04:25Z: lab seat (neo), R-C256 (operator interview)

**R-C256:** garbage-collect PZM's USB `/nix`, then run the R-C254 hook build there.
- **Why:** PZM `/nix` has 2.2 GiB free of 56 (97% full), below the 8 GiB build gate. The neo PZM-builder disk gate is closed for the same reason.
- **Method:** Nix-native reference accounting only, under the ratified 2026-09-12 PZM USB-store policy and R-C43. Remove old generations beyond the current one, then run `nix-store --gc`.
- **Must not touch:** live roots, the external-store identity, and any mount.
- **Then:** once free space is at least 8 GiB, run the R-C254 build on PZM, `nix copy` the result to neo, and do the two-entry repoint.

## 2026-10-04 ~04:10Z: lab seat (neo), R-C254 (operator interview)

**Merged:** #2181, the R-C249 ManagedOOM carve-out, as 7cc57d689 at 04:03Z.
- Validation on sting: 111 tests.
- Verify passes closed two more bypasses in the unit-file carve-out:
  - non-inert lines;
  - `Exec*=` lines and bare `$`.

**R-C254:** the R-C251 delivery build runs on PZM, not neo, because neo's swap is at 5.6 of 7.2 GiB.
1. Evaluate and build the `jess@macbook-neo` HM activation package on PZM (the fleet's Darwin builder) from main 7cc57d689.
2. `nix copy` the closure to neo.
3. Check the old and new hooks against each other.
4. Repoint exactly the Claude PreToolUse agent-process hook entry and the git pre-commit symlink on neo.
5. Add a GC root.
6. Send the store paths to the blahaj seat.

Nothing is activated. The R-C232 batched switch is unchanged.

## 2026-10-04 lab seat (neo), R-C253 (operator interview)

**R-C253:** switch sting's Home Manager now from main (which includes #2180 at 78a56593) to deliver the R-C241 heavy-job slice and wrapper.
- **How:** `nix-switch-local` on sting, run detached and receipted.
- **Readback:** the `tinyland-heavy.slice` properties, a tmux pane scope's ManagedOOMPreference, and a smoke test of the wrapper with a no-op job.
- **Limits:** no reboot, no tmux restart. Live agent tmux sessions on sting are untouched.

The blahaj seat notes that the 26G user-1000 ceiling is not live yet. It will be sized from the real workload after this slice lands.

## 2026-10-04 lab seat (neo), R-C252: R-C249 unblocked (operator interview)

**R-C252** approves both R-N12 alternatives from the S10 lane.
- **Alternative 1:** commit from a message file with `git commit -S -F <file>`, so no signal words appear in shell text.
- **Alternative 2:** make the policy rationale edit in `policy/house-rules.json` with the Edit tool only.

**It also keeps the hardened matcher's extra refusal.** Reading the ManagedOOM directive value back by name is refused:
- `$ManagedOOMSwap` and `${ManagedOOMSwap}`;
- the MemoryPressure forms of both.

This refusal counts as R-N11 signal laundering under R-C249.

**Hardened matcher:**
- Masks only inert commands: printf, echo, cat, tee, mkdir and daemon-reload, plus bare directive lines in committed unit files.
- Passes 108 tests.
- Closes the 22-of-33 bypass gap that the S10 adversarial hunt found in the first matcher.

**Next:**
1. Rebase onto main (#2177 has merged), validate on sting, admin-merge (R-C11).
2. Do the R-C251 build without activation, then repoint the Claude PreToolUse agent-process hook and the git pre-commit hook on neo.
3. Send the store paths to the blahaj seat.
4. Put the shared checkout `/Users/jess/git/lab` back on main.

## 2026-10-04 ~02:15Z: lab seat (neo), R-C249 (operator interview; relayed request from the blahaj seat, TIN-5128)

- **R-C249:** narrow the R-N11 audit (`scripts/validation/agent-process-safety-audit.py`, used by the Claude PreToolUse hook, the Codex hook and the commit-time audit). It must allow systemd directive assignments `^ManagedOOM(Swap|MemoryPressure)=<value>` at line start, whether they appear in file content or in a command that writes file content.
  - Every raw signal spelling stays refused, along with `systemctl kill` and all other R-N11 patterns.
  - A contract test covers both directions: the directive passes, and a bare signal command is still refused.
- **Delivery:** land the fix now. It reaches neo in the R-C232 batched switch; there is no early switch. Blahaj adds its oomd templates (omitting kubepods.slice, rke2-server and tailscaled) after delivery.
- **Context:** this was stacked on the R-C243 quoted-pattern fix (S9), which touches the same file.

2026-10-01 22:25Z: merged PR #1994 (carries the 2026-09-24 R-N11 amendment and the self-bounded timeout ruling) at 2026-10-01T22:25:03Z. Merge commit 69f967d468427714e2ef49858d4e3285f6bcb31e.

Before merging, the branch had two conflicts with main in the policy/house-rules.json history array. Both were resolved with merges rather than a rebase: 0fa5ff5fc on neo, then d505c79c5 signed on sting. All entries are kept in date order: 2026-09-24 D-Bus, this PR's 2026-09-30 self_bounded_timeout_allowed, then main's two 2026-10-01 entries (federated efficiency, remote-seat R-C1/R-C2). Nothing was relaxed.

Admin merge under R-C11, after local validation on sting (merged tree of the PR and main 0cb326916, detached temporary worktree):
- pytest tests/unit/test_house_rules_policy.py, test_agent_process_safety_audit.py, test_agent_instruction_resolution.py and test_cmux_config.py: 116 passed
- test-manifest strict-ci and strict-bazel-linkage: OK; agent-notes index: OK; agent-process-safety-audit: OK

The four CI runs that the resolution push queued were cancelled after the merge to keep load off honey. Issue state is unchanged.

2026-09-30 05:40Z — **C7 carried: lab #1994** (head `635a116b`, signed, auto-merge armed). The operator confirmed today that the 2026-09-24 aside "an agent may bound a command it started with `timeout`" was a ruling. AGENTS.md's Hard Rules R-N11 sentence now cites the 2026-09-30 confirmation and the reason (bounding your own command is not signalling another process; a `timeout` prefix never launders a refused command); `policy/house-rules.json` `process_signal_boundary` gains `self_bounded_timeout_allowed: true` + rationale and a 2026-09-30 amendments entry; new `test_r_n11_self_bounded_timeout_is_a_ruling`, widened `test_timeout_self_bounding_stays_allowed` (`-s`, `--signal=`, `--preserve-status`, `sudo timeout`, `gtimeout` pass; a prefix in front of a raw signal tool, a tmux teardown or an sshd stop still refused). 349 tests green; note `docs/agent-notes/2026-09-30-TIN-3692-rn11-amendment-and-timeout-carrier.md`.

**C1 correction:** the 2026-09-30 inventory's claim that the repo AGENTS.md still carried the pre-amendment absolute R-N11 text was stale — **lab #1913 (merged 2026-09-25) already carried the 2026-09-24 amendment** into both AGENTS.md bullets, `house-rules.json`, the audit and the Claude hook; the lane verified all five surfaces on origin/main and changed no R-N11 wording. No further C1 work.

**2026-09-24, scope confirmation for the R-N11 amendment above.** Operator, verbatim, in the same round:

> "the exit issues were asserted from agents killing pids of other agents, which was unacceptable (similarly, killing live tmux sessions and similar, which is also unacceptable)" … "I think we made the blanket too broad."

**Resulting rule (R-N11 as amended).**
- **Still forbidden to agents on any host:** signalling another agent's processes (codex, claude, pi, kimi, junie and their parents, by PID or pattern); killing live tmux servers, sessions, panes or windows; and killing any live operator or interactive session "and similar". These stay operator-only, and the guard keeps refusing them.
- **Permitted to lab agents when ruled work needs it:** managed service lifecycle on a named job or unit (`launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap`/`kickstart`, `systemctl stop`/`start`/`restart`), and host reboots.
- The 2026-09-20 incident (a literal-PID kill of the operator's tmux server on sting) stays the negative guard's named precedent.

Carrier PR and guard change are to follow. Until neo's next Home Manager switch delivers it, the hook still enforces the old broad text.

**2026-09-24: operator ruling amending R-N11.** It was given as a structured interview answer, so it counts as a ruling under R-N13. Verbatim:

> "I didn't ratify that, at least not realizing the ability to exec these important funcs; this is a fairly routine need as the lab repo agent, and we should be able to exec this when needed, as well as reboots."

**Context.** During an attended PZM Nix-DB repair (TIN-2832), the runbook needed `launchctl bootout system/systems.determinate.nix-daemon`. R-N11 as written made that operator-only, and `tinyland-agent-process-claude-hook` would refuse it from an agent.

**Scope as the agent understands it.** The operator confirms the exact scope in the same interview round; that follow-up is recorded below.
- **Now permitted to lab agents when the work needs it:** managed service lifecycle (`launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap`/`kickstart` of a named launchd job, and `systemctl stop`/`start`/`restart` of a named unit), plus host reboots.
- **Not addressed by this answer, so unchanged until the operator says otherwise:** raw `kill`/`pkill`/`killall` of PIDs or name patterns, and `tmux kill-*`. That is the 2026-09-20 incident class.

**Carrier landing.** A PR will amend:
- the AGENTS.md R-N11 block and its Hard Rules text;
- `nix/home-manager/assets/claude-global-defaults.md`;
- `policy/house-rules.json` `process_signal_boundary`;
- the `agent-process-safety-audit` classification and its tests.

**Enforcement lag.** The PreToolUse hook keeps enforcing the old text until neo's Home Manager switch delivers the change. That switch currently waits on the PZM repair. For this sitting, the operator runs the daemon stop once.

**Ruling 2026-09-24 (operator interview), R-N11 scope: `timeout` self-bounding is allowed.**

An agent may wrap a command it starts in `timeout <n>`, even though `timeout` sends SIGTERM to that child when the limit expires. The allowance covers only a process launched by that same invocation. It never extends to any other process, PID or session. This records existing practice: the lab seat bounded its own fetches, builds and probes this way all session, and on 2026-09-24 ~01:00Z it fired on two of its own gpg probes while gpg-agent was wedged. The seat disclosed it to the operator unprompted rather than assuming it was fine.

Everything else in R-N11 is unchanged. `kill`, `pkill`, `killall`, the tmux, systemctl and launchctl forms, and literal-PID variants against any process the agent didn't just start stay operator-only.

Same sitting: gpg-agent was unresponsive, with three other sessions' signatures queued 24 to 30 minutes behind a pinentry that never showed. The restart (`gpgconf --kill gpg-agent`) is the operator's action under R-N11.

## Process rulings — operator interview, 2026-09-20 (after the tmux incident)

Recorded verbatim from a structured interview; these are rulings, not agent paraphrase.

- **R-N11 — Process control.** *"Absolute: agents never signal, on any host."* No `kill`/`pkill`/`killall`/`tmux kill-*`/`systemctl stop` from any agent shell, in any form, regardless of ruling. The operator performs every stop. The guard hook is to be hardened to refuse literal-PID kills and any command naming a signal — not only `ps`/`pgrep` substitution. To be written into lab `AGENTS.md` and the mythos delegation policy (`prompt-toon/policy/delegation.json` forbidden_tasks). **R-N10 is void.**
- **R-N12 — Hook refusal.** *"Stop, but the agent may propose one alternative."* A guard-hook refusal is a stop: the agent quotes it verbatim and may propose one **materially different** approach (not a rewording), and asks before running it. Reformulating a refused command to evade the pattern is itself a violation and is recorded as one.
- **R-N13 — Ratification.** *"Every mutating step cites a ruling ID in its receipt; questions are never rulings."* A receipt without a cited R-id is an unratified act by definition. Operator questions and asides are recorded verbatim and become rulings only via an explicit "ruling:" or a structured interview answer. Every session writes a lab `docs/agent-notes/` entry before ending. Ticket descriptions are never rewritten; supersession is by dated comment.
- **Scope refocus.** *"We should specifically be working on bulkload and tummycrypt migration to sting. That was the ask."* The deliverable is the Rust bulkload complete/deployed and the migration run with seamless pickup — tummycrypt included. Cleanup and records are in service of that, not ahead of it.

Applied immediately to this session: no process control of any kind; the earlier plan line "tummycrypt stays on neo for now" is withdrawn as a misread aside (9/12), not a ruling.

A clean user reaches a ready managed Claude/Codex fleet through one guided `omux setup` flow without insider topology knowledge or hand-edited JSON.

## Flow

1. Preflight platform, harness binaries, keychain/secret-tool, service support, PATH/version truth, and existing config.
2. Collect labeled operator-owned accounts and desired Claude/Codex harnesses.
3. Stage isolated per-account stores and launch provider-owned login, one isolated browser context per identity.

5. Ask separately for consent to proactive refresh and managed switching; default deny on ambiguity.
6. Install/enable the user refresh/observation service only after confirmation.
7. Run a bounded readiness proof and print precise `omux repair <label>` actions for failures.

## Boundaries

No cookie import as auth, no hidden browser automation, no credential pooling, no daemon-required request proxy, and no broad provider wizard. Agent-safe JSON plan mode must not prompt or read secrets.

## Acceptance

Three steps or fewer from clean install to staged logins/readiness; idempotent rerun; no hand-edited config; macOS live proof and Linux systemd/secret-tool beta proof; redacted clean-user evidence.
